table: candidate envelope rate table, 128 entries, u16 big-endian
source: EOS v4.62 OS image, offset 0x0edd56 in the container payload (payload starts 0x200 after the 0x12345678 header)
IDENTITY_IS_INFERRED: Found by SHAPE, not by matching published values -- E-mu publish no anchors. 128 entries (one per MIDI parameter byte), monotone descending, log-linear. That is consistent with an envelope rate table and is NOT proof it is one. Confirm by changing the parameter on hardware and predicting a value from the entry. See 'selectivity': one distinct candidate in 5689 monotone runs. Still not proof -- no published anchor exists for EOS.
VERSION_CAVEAT: This is 4.62. The bench runs 4.70, whose OS image is packed (RESOLUTION_NOTES 116/122) and cannot be read. Treat as a cross-check, not a reference.
NOT_A_SINGLE_EXPONENTIAL: r2 is 0.99994 over 60-100 and only 0.9895 over the whole table. The ends are steeper (0.128 below byte 20, 0.078 above byte 100). Our law is right where it was fitted and wrong outside it, which is a firmware-side explanation for RESOLUTION_NOTES 105's 'not to be read below ~2 s'.

selectivity.note: All 42 hits are overlapping windows of ONE table present in two byte-identical copies 261396 bytes apart. One distinct candidate in 5689 monotone runs, at a tolerance 25x looser than the match achieved. Counted rather than hedged, at s3ked's suggestion.

IDENTITY_CONFIRMED_2026_09_14: RESOLUTION_NOTES 127. No longer a shape match. With EOS 4.70 decompressed (eosflash), the table's consumer is readable: at body offset 0x3fb38 a routine clamps (rate_field + modulation) >> 5 to 0..127, indexes this table as u16, multiplies by elapsed ticks and adds or subtracts the result from the running envelope level -- the rising and falling branches are the table's only two references. Table[0]=65535 is the largest increment, i.e. instant, matching the 67.1% of corpus rate bytes at byte 0. ALSO: the index is the SUM of a stored field and a modulation term shifted right by 5, so the internal rate resolution is 32x finer than the MIDI byte.
VERSION_CAVEAT_CLOSED: The 256 bytes of this table appear VERBATIM in the decompressed EOS 4.70 image at 0x41490 and 0x1da390 (body offsets). Byte-identical between 4.62 and 4.70, so this is a reading of the firmware the bench runs, not of a neighbouring version.
